title: Product Engineer (Backend/AI) @Briink
description:
What we do

At Briink, we’re building AI technology for the global sustainability economy. We work with the world’s largest climate organizations, including CDP and PRI, and multinational companies such as Bayer, Siemens, Commerzbank, E.ON, and Heidelberg Materials.

Our technology helps automate how sustainability data is collected, analyzed, verified, and acted on. Through our work with global climate organizations, what you build at Briink will directly impact the sustainability workflows of more than 30,000 companies, investors, and cities worldwide.

We’re a small team working at enormous scale. Your code won’t sit behind an internal tool or an experimental demo — it will help shape how some of the world’s largest organizations understand and act on their environmental impact. Based at Berlin’s AI Campus, with a second office in London, and backed by over €7 million in funding, we want to prove that some of the world’s most powerful technology can also be a powerful force for good.

Application requirement: Intro video
As part of your application, please submit a short intro video (max 2 minutes) answering:

  1. Who you are and what you have done/built that is relevant for this role. 
  2. Why you’re excited about owning and shipping AI-powered products at Briink. 
  3. Why Briink’s sustainability mission resonates with you.
Upload your video using this form (YouTube unlisted, Loom, or any other solution is fine). We do this to get a better sense of candidates before continuing the process. Any application without a video will not be considered ;)


Your role

As Briink’s Backend/AI Product Engineer, you’ll join a small, high-ownership product and engineering team building AI-powered products for sustainability professionals.

This is not a narrowly scoped backend role. You’ll take meaningful product problems from initial discovery and user conversations through technical design, implementation, and iteration to deploy them at scale across the ESG market. You’ll combine strong backend and AI/LLM engineering with product judgement and the initiative to work out what should be built - not just how to action a predefined ticket.

You will:

  • Own product features end to end, from understanding the user problem and defining the right approach through to delivery, measurement, and improvement.
  • Design and build scalable backend systems, including APIs, data models, workflows, and infrastructure for complex enterprise products.
  • Build and ship applied AI/LLM features, such as LLM chains, RAG systems, tool-using agents, structured-output pipelines, and evaluation workflows
  • Create reusable, extensible platform building blocks that support multiple user journeys and reporting workflows rather than solving each problem in isolation.
  • Improve the robustness of our systems, strengthening reliability, testing, observability, performance, and maintainability as we scale.
  • Work directly with users, product, and data, using qualitative feedback and product data to understand the real problem and evaluate whether a solution works.
  • Prototype and test new AI capabilities, turning promising ideas into practical product improvements that accelerate our roadmap.
  • Bring thoughtful opinions and constructive challenge, helping the team make better product and technical decisions.
  • Collaborate closely with other engineers, including through pair programming, technical design discussions, and shared problem-solving.


Your profile

Technical requirements

  • Strong professional backend engineering experience, with a track record of designing and shipping reliable production systems.
  • Experience in a small, high-ownership product team, ideally within a startup or scale-up engineering organisation of roughly 5–20 engineers.
  • Evidence that you have shipped meaningful products end to end, rather than owning only a narrow component within a much larger organisation.
  • Strong experience in Python (or another modern backend language such as Java, Ruby, or TypeScript, combined with the ability and willingness to become productive in Python quickly).
  • Strong API, database, and systems design skills, with the ability to model complex workflows and build maintainable foundations for enterprise products.
  • Applied AI/LLM experience: you have experience or a strong interest in LLM-powered features, ideally involving RAG or retrieval, tool use, agents, structured outputs, or evaluation systems.
  • A solid software-quality mindset, including testing, code review, CI/CD, observability, and pragmatic approaches to reliability and security.
  • Cloud and container experience, with an understanding of how to deploy, operate, and scale production workloads.
  • Fluent English (C1+), both written and spoken. 
Nice to have
  • Experience building workflow, reporting, questionnaire, or other complex B2B SaaS products.
  • Familiarity with backend technologies such as FastAPI, PostgreSQL, background queues 
  • Any experience with LangChain, LangSmith, or other LLM frameworks
  • Deeper experience with RAG, retrieval, agents, LLM evaluation, and production AI systems.
  • Experience improving latency, cost, and reliability for AI workloads.
  • Knowledge of ESG, sustainability, climate tech, or corporate reporting.
  • German language skills.
Who you are
  • Kind and collaborative: You treat people well, communicate clearly, and help create a supportive, low-ego team environment.
  • Mission-driven: You care about using technology to accelerate sustainability and climate action.
  • Sharp and curious: You learn quickly, ask good questions, and enjoy getting to the root of difficult product and technical problems.
  • A product-minded builder: You think beyond the task in front of you, focus on the user’s real problem, and care about whether what you ship creates value.
  • Highly self-directed: You thrive in a fast-moving environment with autonomy, ambiguity, and limited oversight.
  • Pragmatic and action-oriented: You can move from ideas to experiments to production without waiting for perfect requirements.
  • Opinionated but open-minded: You challenge ideas constructively, welcome pushback, and enjoy thinking through problems with others.
  • Commercially aware and creative: You balance technical quality with user needs, business value, and speed.
If your experience doesn’t align precisely with all the criteria, don't worry! We encourage you to still apply. Many people miss out on opportunities because they feel they don’t fit every requirement—we believe in attitude, growth and iteration, not perfection!


What we offer

  • Competitive salary and equity, reflecting your impact and ownership.
  • Purpose-driven mission: Build tools that help organisations act more sustainably and make the ESG data ecosystem more transparent.
  • Flexible hybrid setup: Berlin or London based candidates are strongly preferred, with access to our team and the wider startup community at the Merantix AI Campus.
  • Trust and autonomy: Own meaningful problems, shape the product, and influence how we build as the company grows.
  • A genuinely high-impact role: Increase our delivery capacity, strengthen the robustness of our platform, and accelerate product innovation.
  • Dynamic environment: Work in a small, ambitious team at the intersection of applied AI, enterprise software, and sustainability.
  • Learning budget and quarterly hackathons: Explore new technologies and prototype ideas that push Briink forward.
  • A thoughtful hiring process: We are focused on finding the right person, and are willing to take the time needed to do so.

title: Working Student (all genders) – Robust Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction for Dynamic Scene
description:
Abstract

Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models can recover scene geometry directly from images or videos without costly scene-specific optimization. By combining large-scale pre-training, multi-view reasoning, and strong geometric priors, these models provide an efficient alternative to traditional reconstruction pipelines such as Structure-from-Motion, NeRF, and optimization-based 3D Gaussian Splatting.

Despite recent progress, current models remain sensitive to challenging real-world conditions. Occlusions, moving objects, illumination changes, nighttime scenes, reflections, rain, fog, and snow can result in incomplete geometry, unreliable correspondences, and temporally inconsistent predictions. Improving robustness under such conditions is essential for autonomous driving and robotic perception.

As a working student, you will support the development of robust feed-forward reconstruction models for dynamic scenes. You will investigate methods for handling occlusion, changing illumination, and adverse weather, and explore how large reconstruction models can serve as general-purpose geometric backbones for downstream 3D scene understanding, particularly semantic occupancy prediction and 4D occupancy forecasting.


These tasks interest you

  • Develop and evaluate feed-forward 3D reconstruction models for dynamic scenes using monocular or multi-view image sequences.
  • Investigate reconstruction robustness under partial and long-term occlusions, moving objects, and incomplete observations.
  • Develop methods to improve geometric consistency under illumination changes, low-light conditions, shadows, and reflections.
  • Evaluate and improve model performance under adverse weather conditions such as rain, fog, snow, and reduced visibility.
  • Compare the developed methods with relevant baselines and document technical and experimental results.


That makes you stand out

  • You are currently pursuing a degree in computer science, artificial intelligence, robotics, electrical engineering, data science, or a related field.
  • You have excellent programming skills in Python as well as hands-on experience with PyTorch.
  • You have a good understanding of computer vision, deep learning, 3D geometry, or multi-view vision.
  • Experience with depth estimation, optical flow, point clouds, camera pose estimation, NeRF, 3D Gaussian Splatting, or 3D reconstruction is highly beneficial.
  • Your language skills enable you to perform your role in English (at least C1 level). Knowledge of German is desirable but not required.

What you'll do - your playing field

This is how you move our mission forward every day.

  • Data Pipelines: You build and maintain data pipelines for automated data collection, structured so that new sources and markets can be added quickly.
  • Algorithms: You develop algorithms to extract relevant information from websites and images.
  • Data Quality: You ensure data quality through validation, confidence levels, monitoring, and clean handovers internally and to partners.
  • Data Infrastructure: You manage and further develop the data infrastructure of the Teamwear area.

In addition to your core responsibilities, you will also:
  • Internal Tools: You develop internal tools that enable the team to collect and correct data themselves.
  • Analytics & Reports: You create analytics and reports for internal stakeholders and external partners.


What you bring to the team

We're not looking for a perfect CV. But you should recognise yourself in these points.

  • Broad Technical Skillset: You move between data pipelines, backend and some frontend, and are not afraid of AI or image analysis.
  • Data Automation: You have experience with automated data pipelines, web scraping and image processing.
  • Databases & Data Modelling: You have expertise in databases and data modelling.
  • Independent Working: You work independently, even when there is no second engineer in the room and the context comes from business teams.
  • Fast Learner: You quickly get familiar with unfamiliar domains and ask the right questions along the way.

    • A large part of the role is data collection and data quality, rather than greenfield ML. The exciting part is turning messy, real-world sources into reliable data.
    • The area is new. There is no finished setup for you to work with - you will help build it.
    • AI-first: We work AI-first, and AI tools are an active part of our workflow.

Not a must - but this'll definitely earn you extra points.

  • Experience with AWS, Kubernetes or IaC (Pulumi/Terraform). You can also learn this with us.
  • Experience presenting and preparing data for non-technical audiences.

As a Senior Systems Engineer, you will be responsible for the technical outcome of complex space missions.  During mission contracting and requirements development, you may work with the sales engineering org to ensure mission requirements are valid and mission scope is adequately defined. Systems Engineers translate higher level requirements down to lower-level requirements, consulting and collaborating with discipline team-leads and subject matter experts where necessary.    

You will be the overall technical lead responsible for "building the right thing" and "building it right". This will include the management of system requirements, technical budgets, and sub-system interfaces.  Your responsibility extends to ensuring there is sufficient verification and testing of the system, and you will take ownership of the technical performance outcomes for the mission. You will be the mission's technical lead for both Spire-internal and external (customer, contractor, etc) teams, working collaboratively with others to resolve technical discrepancies in requirements, specifications, or system performance.   

You will also act as the technical point of contact for Spire's global customers during mission development phases and through on-orbit validation of the space systems, working with Spire project and program managers to provide effective communication where required.   

Your knowledge and experience working across multiple technical disciplines will help you coordinate Spire's technical efforts to ensure ultimate mission success. 
  

Role Responsibilities:  

  • Take overall technical ownership of Spire Space and/or Ground Systems from technical development through on-orbit verification; ensure that we are "building the right thing" and "building it right". 
  • Lead requirements management for a given mission or program - including development, validation, verification, and change management. 
  • Lead technical risk management for a given mission or program - including identification, qualification, mitigation, and resolution. 
  • Develop top-level requirements and then flow-down to lower-levels, consulting and collaborating with discipline team-leads and subject matter experts where necessary. 
  • Serve as the primary Spire technical POC to customers and contractors - communicating and advocating on behalf of internal technical teams where necessary. 
  • Serve as the customer's technical representative to Spire-internal teams - communicating and sometimes advocating for customer requirements, expectations, and experiences. 
  • Develop working knowledge of Spire's satellite platforms, operations systems, and payloads (both Spire and customer-developed) - including customer APIs and software service interfaces. 
  • Proactively communicate to program/project managers where changes in scope, requirements, expected system performance, or development outcomes impact the mission. 
  • Develop, deliver, and maintain mission documentation required to support programs or missions, including both internal and external (customer- or contractor-facing) documentation. 
  • Support the sales engineering team in the development of technical concepts and budgets, feasibility assessments, requirements, scope, and documentation needed during the sales cycle.  

Basic Qualifications:  

  • BSc in Engineering, Computer Science, equivalent STEM-related subject, or equivalent work experience. 
  • 5+ years of experience working in a technical engineering discipline (Mechanical, Electrical, Software, Controls, RF Communications, etc) or as a systems engineer for complex integrated systems. 
  • Comprehensive understanding of space systems, concepts of operations, and remote systems operation.  

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • 3+ years of experience as a space systems engineer working across engineering disciplines (Mechanical, Electrical, Software, Controls, Radio/Comms, etc) 
  • Experience developing or integrating RF and optical payloads. 
  • Experience participating in architecture and design of digital systems including ground station networks, data distribution and data processing systems, and spacecraft data handling systems 
  • Experience coordinating or leading diverse technical teams spanning multiple engineering disciplines and time zones 
  • Strong interpersonal skills for building relationships with clients and effectively communicating with other members of cross-functional teams 
  • Strong comprehension skills to enable timely understanding of complex customer requirements and identification of thorough and sometimes unique solutions 
  • Experience in satellite mission design, development, and testing with a clear understanding of major mission design trades and scope drivers (power / payload duty cycle, communications systems / data budgets, ground stations, launch and environmental loads, EMI/EMC, thermal management, etc.)

  • Work hands-on with the DevOps team to implement GCP organizational policies, IAM least-privilege architectures, and Cloud Armor (WAF/rate limiting).

We are a remote-first company with teams located around the Globe.

  • You prioritize by real-world risk, propose trade-offs rather than demanding perfection, and communicate complex risks plainly to engineers and leadership.

Become part of Tanso and decarbonize industries with us.

What if the impact of your role extended beyond a job title?

Not through marketing spin. Not through vague "purpose-driven" messaging. But through software that helps industrial companies understand, manage and actively reduce their environmental impact.

That's what Tanso is building. And it's one of the reasons people join us.


Why Tanso?

  • Take Action in a Fast-Moving, High-Impact Environment. We move fast on sustainability because the urgency is real. That means decisions that matter, transparent processes, and the agility to navigate change.
  • Challenge & Grow Through Ownership. Take ownership immediately, build expertise through hands-on experience, and leverage every available resource to achieve outsized impact.
  • Foster Trust with Mission-Driven Collaborators. You'll join a team that prioritizes impact and each other. We give honest feedback, share credit, support each other when it matters, and hold high standards together.
  • Embrace Responsibility & Drive Impact. Turn fragmented emissions data into actionable insights. Your work has immediate, visible impact - clearer decision-making and genuine momentum toward change.
  • AI First-Mindset. We embrace cutting-edge technology to solve sustainability challenges. Push the boundaries of innovation and stay ahead of what's possible.
  • Commitment to Performance & Excellence. We cultivate a high-performance culture where you thrive. Push yourself and others to excel, celebrate wins, learn from setbacks, and raise the bar.


Your role

To take real ownership of what you build and take own end-to-end feature responsibility, we are looking for a Software Engineer (f/m/x). 

As a Software Engineer (m/f/x)  you will work on meaningful customer-facing problems within one of our platform modules and collaborate closely with product, design, customer success, and other engineers.

At Tanso, engineers are responsible understanding the problem, challenging assumptions, shaping the solution, making technical trade-offs, shipping to production, and iterating based on what we learn. We care less about following a predefined playbook and more about making good decisions, moving with purpose, and building software that creates tangible value for our customers.


Key responsibilities

  • Own customer-facing features from problem definition through implementation, rollout, and iteration.
  • Turn ambiguous requirements and user needs into pragmatic, maintainable solutions. Challenge assumptions and help decide what is worth building
  • Collaborate closely with product designers and customer success to understand user needs and shape effective solutions.
  • Contribute to the quality of our codebase, engineering practices, and developer experience.


Your profile

  • You have 2+ years of professional software engineering experience building and shipping production software in Typescript.
  • Strong full-stack and product thinking, understanding systems end-to-end.
  • First experience with backend development, ideally with PostgreSQL and Azure.
  • Clear, precise communicator in English. 
  • Self-driven problem solver with strong ownership and execution mindset.
Nice to have
  • German language skills. 


What we offer

  • A highly competitive compensation package with an attractive equity package to participate in Tanso's growth. 
  • Hybrid working model that combines the benefits of onsite collaboration with the flexibility needed. 
  • A company-contributed pension plan to support long-term financial security. 
  • Yearly budget to support ongoing professional development. 
  • Sponsored access to EGYM Wellpass to prioritize your wellbeing with thousands of options. 
  • Exclusive discounts that help you save on a wide range of everyday brands, services, and experiences. 


Our team

We're a diverse group of people, and that diversity is what makes us great. We bring unique perspectives to everything we do and are always eager to learn from each other. We work in cross-functional teams to tackle ambitious challenges, actively seek feedback and be the best versions of ourselves.

title: Head of Engineering (m/f/d)
description:
What we are building

ecoplanet builds the operating system for the energy transition. Our software helps European businesses cut energy costs, run more efficiently, and take the pain out of managing energy day to day. We are around 40 people and backed by EQT Ventures, HV Capital and others.


Why This Role Matters

You lead engineering at ecoplanet: 11 engineers in two squads, including two squad leads.

This is the most senior engineering role in the company. There is no CTO above you. You own the technical direction, not just the delivery of someone else's plan, and you are the engineering voice on the leadership team.

It is also a hands-on job. With a team this size you stay close to the code and the architecture. If you have been away from technical work for a few years, this might not be the right role for you.

What you will own:

  • The team. 11 engineers, which includes two engineering managers. Hiring, performance, growth, and keeping good people
  • The systems. Our Cockpit SaaS platform, the metering and IoT integration layer, the data platform (time-series ingestion, quality, pipelines), the forecasting and optimization services, and the automation that acts on customer assets
  • The technical direction. Architecture, build-vs-buy, and the big platform calls
  • Delivery. Quarterly roadmap execution, owned together with Product
  • Operations. Reliability, on-call, incidents, security posture, and cloud spend


What You’ll Achieve

  • Get the best out of the team you have and grow only where it clearly adds. At 11 people, losing one strong engineer costs more than one extra hire gains. But you should be capable of growing the team substantially if business demands it
  • Turn the roadmap into commitments the company can count on. Surface dependencies early, clear blockers, and make the trade-off calls with Product and the founders.
  • We expect engineering to care about business and product and we expect you to be an example here
  • Set the architecture so it holds as data volume, customer count and the team grow.
  • Run incidents properly: fast response, honest postmortems, fixes that stop the same thing happening again
  • Keep enough processes to be reliable and no more. A 11-person team should not feel like a 100-person one
  • Work closely with Product, Data Science, our energy market experts and other disciplines, so we build against the real physical and regulatory constraints


What Sets You Up for Success

Must have

  • 3+ years of experience leading engineering teams before in a product company, including senior engineers or squad leads
  • You have done it in a lean team, hands-on, without a layer of managers to delegate to. Some excellent large-company leaders struggle here. There is no layer to hide behind
  • You have personally owned delivery predictability and reliability for a production system real customers depend on, and you can tell us what it looked like before and after
  • Strong technical judgment in at least two of: cloud and distributed backend / multi-tenant SaaS; high-volume or time-series data pipelines; IoT, device integration and real-time telemetry; ML or optimization in production. Deep enough to earn engineers' trust, make architecture calls and set the technical direction yourself
  • You have run hiring and performance for real: you have grown people, and you have also managed people out when that was the right call
  • You treat incident management, security and compliance as yours to own, not to delegate
  • Clear written and spoken English. German is a strong plus — most of our customers are German Mittelstand
Nice to have
  • Energy, industrial, SaaS or a physical-world domain.
  • Having been the most senior technical person somewhere before (CTO, VP Engineering, or the person everyone asked).
Not required
  • Being the strongest coder on the team. You do need to read the code, make architecture calls, and occasionally build something.
  • A “Head of” title already. We look at what you have done, not what it was called.


What You Get

  • Top-of-market team, flat hierarchy — work alongside people who push you to get better
  • Competitive salary
  • Full ownership from day one — you actively shape our company
  • Central office, easy commute — free lunch every Tuesday and Thursday
  • Wellpass membership
  • Regular 1:1s and retros focused on your growth
  • Real impact — your work supports Europe's transition to a smarter energy system

title: Data Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
What we are building

At ecoplanet, we're redefining energy for tomorrow. Our mission: turn energy management into the competitive edge every European business relies on to win its market. We're building the operating system for the energy transition — cutting energy costs, improving efficiency, and streamlining operations. Backed by EQT Ventures, HV Capital and more, and built by a team full of top-tier talent.


Why This Role Matters

You will build and run the data backbone the whole product sits on. Meter readings arrive from industrial sites across Europe, through messages or us accessing APIs. Your job is to get that data in clean, on time, and in a shape that dashboards, insights and forecasts can rely on.

You will join a team of 12 engineers in two squads. Small team, real ownership, and what you build reaches customers in weeks rather than quarters.


What You’ll Achieve

  • Meter data integration. Connect industrial hardware and utility data streams into real-time dashboards. Every site is a little different, so a good part of the job is bringing data into a consistent structure across all sites
  • Anomalies and insights. This is where data science comes in. Find the things in the data a customer would want to know about — a meter drifting, a machine left running overnight, consumption that does not fit the pattern — and turn them into something they can act on
  • Tech stack and growth. Support the engineering team building scalable data pipeline


What Sets You Up for Success

Must have:

  • At least 3–5 years in a data engineering role or something close to it, building pipelines other people depend on

  • Hands-on data science experience. You do not need a research background. You do need to have built and evaluated models yourself: enough to tell a real anomaly from noise, to judge when a finding is solid enough to put in front of a paying customer, and to know what a pipeline owes a model running in production

  • Solid with Python and SQL and cloud data infrastructure. You have designed and run pipelines, APIs and workflows in production

  • Comfortable with high-volume time-series data: ingestion, data quality, backfills, and the everyday reality of late, missing and duplicated readings

  • You think end to end before you go deep. When you hit a hard problem, the first instinct we want is “can a change somewhere else in the chain make this easy?” rather than heading straight into solving the hard version. A company our size cannot afford clever answers to problems that did not need solving

  • Clear written and spoken English. German is a plus

Nice to have:

  • Energy, industrial, IoT or another domain where the data comes off real hardware

  • Metering or device protocols, telemetry at scale, or streaming pipelines

  • Knowledge of a second programming language, like TypeScript or Kotlin

  • You run what you build: monitoring, alerting, and the occasional early morning debugging a pipeline


What You Get

  • Top-of-market team, flat hierarchy — work alongside people who push you to get better
  • Competitive salary
  • Full ownership from day one — you actively shape our company
  • Close collaboration with our Product team
  • Central office, easy commute — free lunch every Tuesday and Thursday
  • Wellpass membership
  • Regular 1:1s and retros focused on your growth
  • Real impact — your work supports Europe's transition to a smarter energy system

title: Software Engineer (Founding Team)
description:
Warum es junini gibt

Brillen kauft man seit hundert Jahren auf die gleiche Art: einmal viel Geld auf den Tisch legen und dann mehrere Jahre mit dem Ergebnis leben. Das Brillenabo ändert das. KundInnen bekommen die Brillen, die sie wirklich brauchen, flexibel und zu planbaren monatlichen Kosten. In Skandinavien ist das längst normal, dort setzt der Markt über 300 Millionen Euro im Jahr damit um. In Deutschland kann es bisher nur anbieten, wer eine eigene Softwareabteilung hat. Für rund 8.000 Einzeloptiker und die regionalen Ketten ist es damit unerreichbar.

Wir bauen die Lösung, mit der jeder Optiker ein Brillenabo anbieten kann, von der Kette mit 200 Filialen bis zum Einzeloptiker in der Fußgängerzone. Unser Ziel ist die Marktführerschaft für Brillenabos in Europa, in einer Branche, die seit Jahrzehnten kaum Innovation gesehen hat.

Wo wir stehen

Die Plattform ist entwickelt, die erste Optikerkette geht im Oktober live. Die Finanzierung steht und erlaubt uns, nachhaltig auf profitables Wachstum zu setzen. Der Schritt in weitere europäische Märkte ist für das nächste Jahr geplant.

Aufgaben

Die Rolle

Du bist der erste Engineer neben unserem CTO. Keine Legacy-Systeme, keine Prozesse, die dich bremsen.

  • Production Readiness: Gemeinsam mit dem CTO verantwortest Du die Plattform im Live-Betrieb und entwickelst sie kontinuierlich weiter.
  • Produktverantwortung: Du übernimmst ganze Bereiche der Plattform und entwickelst sie eigenständig weiter.
  • Technische Entscheidungen: Architektur, Stack, Build und Deploy. Du entscheidest mit.
  • Direkt am Kunden: Mittelfristig betreust du eigene Optiker und baust auf Basis dessen, was du dort lernst.
  • AI-first Engineering: Du prägst, wie wir mit KI entwickeln, testen und ausliefern.

Unser Stack

Kotlin und Java mit Spring Boot, React mit TypeScript, AWS mit RDS, GitHub Actions, dazu Integrationen für Auth, Payments und die Warenwirtschaft unserer Optiker.

Qualifikation

Was du mitbringst

  • Zwei bis vier Jahre als Software Engineer mit Schwerpunkt Backend. Idealerweise hast du Erfahrung mit Java/Kotlin und Spring Boot.
  • Cloud: Du hast Anwendungen nicht nur gebaut, sondern auch deployed und im Betrieb betreut.
  • React: weit genug, um ein Feature end-to-end zu liefern, statt auf jemanden zu warten.
  • Deutsch: gut genug für ein Gespräch mit einem Optiker. Perfekt muss es nicht sein, aber du willst früh eigene Kunden betreuen. B2-Niveau oder besser.
  • Umsetzung vor Diskussion: Du entscheidest lieber und korrigierst später. Mit einer Lösung, die nur okay ist, bist du nicht zufrieden.
  • Low Ego

Benefits

Wie wir arbeiten

  • Prozesse aufnehmen. Du sprichst mit den Menschen, die einen Prozess täglich durchlaufen – bei uns oder beim Kunden. Du hältst fest, wie er heute wirklich läuft (nicht, wie er laut Handbuch laufen sollte), wo Zeit verloren geht und was am Ende besser sein soll.

Dazu:

ENUSEN ist eine junge Nutrition-Marke aus Deutschland mit einer klaren Idee: moderne Ernährung soll zu echten Lebensmomenten passen – unkompliziert, hochwertig und relevant für Menschen mit einem aktiven Alltag.

Mit Smart Balance entwickeln wir aktuell unsere erste Produktlinie – eine neue Form moderner Daily Nutrition zwischen klassischem Snack und vollständiger Mahlzeit.

Für den Aufbau unserer Marke und den bevorstehenden Marktlaunch suchen wir eine Persönlichkeit, die Social Media nicht nur verwaltet, sondern eine junge Marke sichtbar macht, eine Community aufbaut und Menschen für sie begeistert.

Aufgaben

Deine Rolle

Als Social Media & Brand Growth Manager (m/w/d) gestaltest du den Social-Media-Auftritt von ENUSEN von Anfang an mit.

Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit unserem Head of Brand & Growth relevante Content-Formate, baust unsere Social-Media-Kanäle und Community auf und entwickelst ein Netzwerk aus Creatorn, Influencern und Markenbotschaftern.

Dabei suchen wir ausdrücklich keinen reinen Strategen. Wir möchten jemanden, der Ideen entwickelt und sie auch selbst umsetzt.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Aufbau und Weiterentwicklung unserer Social-Media-Kanäle, insbesondere Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, LinkedIn und YouTube
  • Entwicklung von Content- und Redaktionsplänen passend zur Brand- und Launchstrategie
  • Konzeption und Umsetzung von Social-Media-Content, Reels, Short Videos, Stories und weiteren digitalen Formaten
  • Aufbau und Betreuung eines Creator-, UGC- und Influencer-Netzwerks
  • Identifikation, Ansprache und Koordination geeigneter Creator und Kooperationspartner
  • Entwicklung von Creator Briefings und Begleitung von Kooperationen von der Idee bis zur Veröffentlichung
  • Aufbau und aktive Weiterentwicklung unserer Community
  • Planung und Begleitung von Foto-, Video-, Interview- und Content-Produktionen
  • Unterstützung bei PR, Brand Partnerships, Events, Sampling- und Launch-Aktivitäten
  • Zusammenarbeit mit externen Agenturen, Freelancern und Dienstleistern
  • Beobachtung relevanter Social-, Consumer- und Content-Trends
  • Analyse der Performance unserer Inhalte und kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung auf Basis relevanter KPIs
  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Brand & Growth, E-Commerce und Geschäftsführung

Qualifikation

Dein Profil

  • 2-5 Jahre relevante Berufserfahrung im Bereich Social Media, Influencer/Creator Marketing, Content, Community oder Brand Communication
  • Erfahrung mit Influencer Marketing, Creator Relations und UGC
  • Sehr gutes Verständnis für Instagram, TikTok und aktuelle Content-Formate
  • Du kannst nicht nur Konzepte schreiben, sondern Inhalte und Kampagnen auch praktisch umsetzen
  • Sicheres Gespür für Sprache, Storytelling, Bildwelten und Markenkommunikation
  • Erfahrung mit Tools wie Canva, CapCut, Premiere Pro oder vergleichbaren Anwendungen ist von Vorteil
  • Idealerweise Erfahrung in Nutrition, Consumer Health, Food, FMCG, Beauty, Lifestyle oder D2C
  • Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem bzw. C2-Niveau und sehr gutes Englisch
  • Eigeninitiative, Kreativität und Freude daran, Strukturen nicht nur zu übernehmen, sondern selbst mit aufzubauen

Benefits

Was wir bieten

  • Die Möglichkeit, eine neue Consumer Brand von Beginn an aktiv mitzugestalten
  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit unserem Head of Brand & Growth und der Geschäftsführung
  • Kurze Entscheidungswege und viel eigener Gestaltungsspielraum
  • Verantwortung statt starrer Konzernstrukturen
  • Ein Arbeitsumfeld, in dem gute Ideen schnell umgesetzt werden können
  • Zusätzlich Teilnahme an unserem Performance-Bonus-Pool, orientiert an individueller Leistung sowie dem Beitrag zum Unternehmens- und Absatzwachstum
  • Langfristige Entwicklungs- und Wachstumsmöglichkeiten gemeinsam mit ENUSEN

Was uns besonders wichtig ist

ENUSEN befindet sich noch am Anfang. Deshalb suchen wir keinen Menschen, der lediglich einen bestehenden Social-Media-Kalender weiterführt.

Wir suchen jemanden, der Freude daran hat, zu sagen:

„Ich war dabei, als diese Marke aufgebaut wurde.“

Du solltest Lust darauf haben, Dinge auszuprobieren, Verantwortung zu übernehmen, nah am Produkt und am Konsumenten zu arbeiten und gemeinsam mit einem kleinen Team aus einer Idee eine relevante Consumer Brand zu entwickeln.

Interesse?

Dann freuen wir uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.

Bitte sende uns deinen Lebenslauf sowie – sofern vorhanden – gerne Beispiele von Social-Media-Kanälen, Content-Projekten, Creator-Kampagnen oder Marken, an denen du bereits gearbeitet hast.

title: Videograf / Content Producer (m/w/d)
description:
SKINBRO ist eine der am schnellsten wachsenden Männerpflege-Marken Deutschlands. Feste Duschseifen, Deos und Parfums – plastikfrei, made in Germany, mit Düften, die Männer wirklich wollen. Über 90.000 Kunden, in den letzten Monaten jeden Monat fast verdoppelt. Wir sitzen in Hamburg, sind ein kleines, schnelles Team und wachsen ohne Konzernstrukturen.

Unser Wachstum kommt aus Creatives. Aktuell produzieren wir rund 300 Ads im Monat mit einem Shooting pro Woche. Mit dir wollen wir auf drei Shootings pro Woche und über 1.000 Assets im Monat.

Spoiler: Wir suchen keinen klassischen Videografen und keinen Creative Director. Wir suchen die Person, die Ideen in die Realität bringt. Die Creative Strategie – Konzepte, Skripte, Angles, Briefings – kommt fertig vom Gründer. Du bekommst am Anfang der Woche deine Shooting-Pläne und ziehst sie von A bis Z durch. Um dich herum: externe Video-Editoren, ein Grafikdesigner, ein eingespielter Prozess.

Das ist eine ausführende Rolle, keine konzeptionelle. Wenn du lieber selbst die Strategie machen willst, ist das nicht die richtige Stelle. Wenn du Bock hast, in einer Creative-Maschine zu arbeiten, die bereits funktioniert, und sie mit uns zu verdreifachen – dann schon.

Aufgaben

Du führst 2–3 Shootings pro Woche eigenständig durch – ohne dass der Gründer am Set stehen muss.

Du organisierst alles drumherum: Location, Darsteller, UGC-Creator, Zeitplan, Equipment, Verpflegung.

Du sourcst regelmäßig neue Gesichter für Straßeninterviews, Schauspieler-Spots und UGC.

Du bedienst die Kamera selbst und lieferst sauberes, verwertbares Rohmaterial nach Briefing.

Du legst das Material strukturiert ab und übergibst es mit klarem Briefing an unsere Editoren.

Du gibst den Editoren fundiertes Feedback und schneidest bei Bedarf selbst.

Du analysierst gemeinsam mit dem Gründer, welche Creatives performt haben und welche nicht – und nimmst die Learnings mit ins nächste Shooting.

Qualifikation

Du kannst Shootings komplett selbstständig durchführen – Planung, Dreh, Ablage.

Du kannst editieren (Premiere, CapCut, DaVinci o. ä.) – gut genug, um Editoren präzise zu briefen, ihr Ergebnis zu bewerten und selbst Videos zu schneiden.

Du hast Feingefühl am Set: Du empfängst Leute, machst sie locker, korrigierst taktvoll und sorgst dafür, dass alle gerne wiederkommen – auch bei Skripten, die etwas frecher sind.

Du hast ein Gespür dafür, welche Person welche Aussage am glaubwürdigsten rüberbringt.

Du arbeitest strukturiert nach Prozess und Checkliste und hast kein Problem damit, Content in hoher Frequenz zu produzieren, ohne dass die Qualität leidet.

Du verstehst, was eine Performance-Ad von einem schönen Video unterscheidet – oder willst es schnell lernen.

Du wohnst in Hamburg oder bist bereit, hierher zu ziehen.

Benefits

Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit dem Gründer-Team.
Ads, die jeden Monat Millionen von Männern sehen – du siehst sofort, was dein Output bewirkt.

Keine Konzernstrukturen, kurze Wege, schnelle Entscheidungen.

Büro direkt in der Hamburger-Innenstadt.

In der Welt des IT-Handels gehen wir neue Wege: Das größte Sortiment, persönliche Beratung und tiefgehende Lösungskompetenz – aus einer Hand.

description:

Zum Ausbau unseres AI- und Automatisierungsbereichs suchen wir dich als AI Automation Engineer – Marketing & Operations Consulting (m/w/d).

So werden aus Möglichkeiten messbar eingesparte Stunden.
Infos unter www.klickpiloten.de.
 
Deine Aufgaben

  • Bauen und betreiben: Du entwickelst unsere internen KI-Systeme weiter – Assistenten, Agenten, automatisierte Workflows – vom ersten Prototyp bis in den produktiven Betrieb. Du baust selbst, mit Claude Code, Cursor oder womit auch immer du am schnellsten zum Ergebnis kommst. Und du hältst am Leben, was du gebaut hast: Monitoring, Fehlerfälle, Kosten, Qualität der Ergebnisse. Schnell gebaut heißt bei uns nicht wegwerfbar.
  • Systeme verbinden, Kontext schaffen: Du verdrahtest unsere Werkzeuge miteinander – Google Ads API, Meta Marketing API, SEO-Tools, unser CRM, Google Workspace, MCP-Server. Du sorgst dafür, dass unsere KI-Systeme mit den richtigen Daten arbeiten. Das ist der eigentliche Hebel: Ein Modell ist nur so gut wie der Kontext, den es bekommt.
  • Kundenprojekte und Marketing Technology: Du berätst unsere Kund*innen zu ihrem Marketing-Technology-Stack: welche Systeme sie wirklich brauchen, wie Shop, CRM und Werbeplattformen zusammenspielen, wo Datenfeeds und Schnittstellen hingehören.   • Tracking, Consent und Analytics: Du baust Tracking- und Analytics-Setups auf, bringst das Consent Management sauber dazu und konsolidierst vor allem Marketingdaten aus ihren vielen Quellen – Werbeplattformen, SEO-Tools, Shop, CRM – zu einem Bild, das trägt. Du automatisierst, was daraus regelmäßig entstehen muss: die Präsentation, die sich aus Kampagnendaten selbst zusammenbaut, das Reporting, das Dienstagfrüh fertig im Sheet steht. Und du bleibst nicht bei der Zahl stehen, sondern liest aus den Daten, was sie über Kampagnen, Zielgruppen und Budgets sagen, und machst daraus eine Empfehlung, mit der Teams und Kund*innen etwas anfangen können.

Abweichungen fallen auf, bevor eine Kundin sie bemerkt. Aus wiederkehrenden Fehlerbildern machst du Regeln, die dauerhaft mitlaufen.
  • Enablement und Coaching: Du schulst und begleitest die Teams, fortlaufend und nah an der konkreten Arbeit statt im einmaligen Workshop. Du schreibst Playbooks, Anleitungen und Dokumentation, die auch jemand versteht, der nicht dabei war. Und du erkennst, welche Handarbeit sich zu automatisieren lohnt und welche man besser Handarbeit sein lässt.
  • Compliance, Datenschutz und Vertraulichkeit: Du entscheidest mit, welche KI-Anbieter und Modelle wir einsetzen und wo Kundendaten dabei landen dürfen. Damit wir uns gegenseitig keine Zeit nehmen:
  • Keine reine Beratungsrolle. Du berätst Kund*innen, aber du baust jede Woche auch selbst.
  • Kein klassischer Entwicklerjob. Du sitzt nicht im abgeschirmten Sprint, sondern zwischen Fachteams und Kund*innen.

  • Praxis mit LLM-APIs: Tool Use, strukturierte Ausgaben, Embeddings, das Bewerten von Ergebnisqualität und ein Gefühl für Token-Kosten.
  • Digitalmarketing-Verständnis. Du weißt, was eine Kampagnenstruktur ist, was ein Sichtbarkeitsindex aussagt und warum Attribution kompliziert ist.
  • Sicherheit in Web Analytics: Du kannst ein sauberes, einwilligungskonformes Tracking-Setup aufbauen, Datenquellen zusammenführen und aus dem Ergebnis eine Empfehlung ableiten – nicht nur ein Dashboard bauen.

  • Deutsch als Muttersprache und sicheres Englisch für jede Dokumentation.
  • Bereitschaft zu gelegentlichen Terminen bei Kund*innen und an unseren anderen Standorten.

title: Werkstudent:in Text & Content (m/w/d)
description:

Wir suchen die Person, die das ändert. Nicht mehr Kanäle, nicht mehr Reichweite sondern bessere Worte für gute Arbeit.

Für wen Du schreibst

Geschäftsführer:innen, Bereichsleitungen und Werkleiter mittelständischer Unternehmen: Maschinenbau, Versicherung, Logistik, Handel. Sie haben viel über KI gehört und wenig gesehen, das im Alltag funktioniert. Sie lesen keine englischen Buzzwords und sie haben nur fünf Minuten.

Für diese Leute zu schreiben ist eine eigene Disziplin. Ein Ton daneben, und der Text ist weg. Genau darum geht es in dieser Rolle: den Kopf von jemandem einnehmen, der völlig anders arbeitet als Du, und dann in seinen Worten schreiben statt in unseren.

Aufgaben

Cases schreiben. Der Kern der Rolle. Du sprichst mit den Kolleg:innen, die ein Projekt gebaut haben, teils auch mit dem Kunden, und machst daraus eine Geschichte, die eine Fremde in vier Minuten versteht: Was war das Problem, was haben wir gebaut, was ist seitdem anders. Das Material liegt da. Es ist nur noch niemand hingegangen und hat es aufgeschrieben.

Die Website texten. Unsere Seite wird gerade neu gebaut. Struktur und Technik machen andere. Die Worte machst Du: Startseite, Leistungsseiten, Cases, Karriereseite. Du pflegst sie danach auch selbst im CMS ein, das lernst Du an einem Nachmittag.

Bestehendes überarbeiten. Pitch-Decks, Newsletter, Lead Magnets, LinkedIn-Posts, Vortragsunterlagen. Vieles davon ist inhaltlich richtig und sprachlich zu lang, zu vage oder zu sehr aus unserer Sicht erzählt. Du gehst da durch und machst es besser.

Schreiben, was in unseren Kanälen steht. Newsletter, Webinare, LinkedIn und unsere Inbox sind die Orte, an denen Deine Texte bei echten Menschen ankommen. Du bedienst die Werkzeuge nicht, Du lieferst den Inhalt: das Skript für ein Webinar, den Newsletter-Text, die Antwortvorlagen, mit denen wir auf eingehende Anfragen reagieren. Versand, Takt und Datenpflege in HubSpot und HeyReach liegen woanders - außer du hast Lust es zu lernen.

Dafür bekommst Du Zugriff auf unsere LinkedIn-Inbox und auf Aufzeichnungen echter Kundengespräche. Nicht als Vertriebsaufgabe, sondern als Materialquelle: Dort steht, wie unsere Kunden über ihr Problem sprechen. Genau diese Worte gehören in unsere Texte.

Optional ist die Visualisierung deiner Arbeit in Form von Präsentationen, Canva-Designs oder Webseiten.

Woran wir nach drei Monaten sehen, dass es funktioniert

  • Vier Cases sind live + der Vertrieb schickt sie tatsächlich an Interessenten.
  • Die neuen Website-Texte stehen und klingen nach uns und unserer Arbeit.
  • Jemand aus dem Team schickt Dir seinen Text vorher zum Drüberlesen, weil er danach besser ist.

Qualifikation

  • Du bist immatrikuliert. Welches Fach, ist uns egal.
  • Du schreibst Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau. Nicht nur fehlerfrei, sondern gut: Rhythmus, Kürze, der richtige Ton für den jeweiligen Leser.
  • Du kannst Dich beim Schreiben in Deine Zielgruppe hineinversetzen.
  • Du hast schon einmal etwas geschrieben, das andere gelesen haben. Studierendenzeitung, Newsletter, der Instagram-Kanal eines Vereins, ein Blog, den es seit zwei Jahren gibt.
  • Du bist in Berlin oder ziehst gerade her. Wir arbeiten hybrid, mittwochs sehen wir uns.

Was Du nicht brauchst

Kein Marketing- oder Kommunikationsstudium. Keine Agenturerfahrung. Kein Portfolio. Keine Design- oder Programmierkenntnisse, keine SEO-Zertifikate, keine Erfahrung mit KI-Tools. Was ein Sprachmodell kann und wo es Unsinn erzählt, lernst Du hier in der ersten Woche, an echter Arbeit statt in einem Kurs.

Erfahrung mit Mittelstandskunden brauchst Du auch nicht. Neugier auf sie schon.

Du passt zu uns, wenn

  • … Dich ein schlechter Satz körperlich stört und Du ihn umschreibst, statt darüber zu diskutieren.
  • … Du Dich für Themen begeistern kannst, über die auf LinkedIn niemand spricht: Schadenregulierung, Ersatzteillogistik, Angebotskalkulation und wie KI diese verändert.
  • … Du lieber fünf Fragen stellst, bevor Du anfängst, als hinterher zu erklären, wie es gemeint war.
  • … Du einen Text abgibst, wenn er gut ist, und nicht erst, wenn er perfekt ist.

Diese Rolle ist nichts für Dich, wenn

  • … Du Redaktionspläne, Kanalstrategien und Reportings bauen willst. Das ist hier nicht die Arbeit.
  • … Du für die Startup- und Tech-Bubble schreiben willst. Unsere Leser:innen sitzen in Unternehmen, die es seit vierzig Jahren gibt.
  • … Du nur über das schreiben willst, was Du selbst spannend findest.
  • … Du Feedback an Deinem Text als Kritik an Dir liest. Hier wird jeder Text angefasst, auch der vom Gründer.

Benefits

Deine Worte gehen live. Was Du schreibst, steht wenige Tage später auf der Website oder liegt bei einem Kunden auf dem Tisch. Keine Freigabekette, keine Marketingabteilung über Dir.

Nähe zu echten Kunden. Du schreibst nicht über eine Persona. Du hörst den Leuten zu, für die Du schreibst, und benutzt danach ihre Worte statt unserer.

KI-natives Schreiben, bevor es alle können. Du arbeitest mit Claude, ChatGPT und Cursor an echter Arbeit und lernst dabei den Teil, der schwerer ist als Prompten: erkennen, wann ein Text nach Maschine klingt, und ihn zurückholen. Die meisten Deiner Kommiliton:innen lernen das im ersten Job nach dem Studium. Oder auch nicht.

Ein Gegenüber. Du bekommst Feedback an Deinen Texten, wöchentlich und im Detail. Das ist der Grund, warum diese Rolle mehr bringt als ein Werkstudentenjob in einer großen Marketingabteilung.

Der Rahmen. Büro im EDGE Coworking am Hauptbahnhof, mittwochs Team-Tag, den Rest teilst Du Dir ein. In Klausurenphasen reduzieren, in den Semesterferien aufstocken.

Perspektive. Werkstudierende sind für uns keine günstige Zusatzkapazität, sondern die Pipeline für feste Rollen. Wenn es passt, gibt es nach dem Studium eine realistische Perspektive bei uns.

Lucid Labs ist ein AI-first Studio für angewandte KI im deutschen Mittelstand. Wir beraten nicht nur bei der Auswahl von Anwendungsfällen, sondern bauen und betreiben Lösungen, die produktiv in echten Prozessen laufen. Von der Idee bis zum Piloten beim Kunden dauert es bei uns rund eine Woche. Gründer Marek Janetzke hat zuvor Flightright mit aufgebaut und bis zum erfolgreichen Exit begleitet.

Unsere Kultur in einem Satz: Mitdenken statt abarbeiten. Klartext statt Buzzwords. Umsetzen statt Folienschlacht.

  2. Eine kleine Aufgabe, rund zwanzig Minuten: Geh auf unsere Webseite, such Dir einen Absatz, der Dir nicht gefällt, und schreib ihn so um, dass eine Geschäftsführerin aus dem Maschinenbau ihn in dreißig Sekunden versteht. Begünde kurz.

At Moss, we give finance professionals the power to automate their day-to-day and make forward-thinking decisions.

Our team and culture make us unique — we’re driven by impact and growth, where every one of us strives to learn and excel. Recognised by Sifted’s Rising 100 and LinkedIn's Top Startups, we’re here to help propel your career and together, make Moss a lasting success.

We're hiring a Pricing & Deal Desk Manager within the Revenue Operations team. You'd take ownership of one of Moss's highest-leverage commercial functions: the pricing deal desk. It's already delivered real results, and it matters more every quarter as deal volume grows and Moss moves into bigger, more complex deals.

What makes the role unusual is that the desk already runs on AI. An agent picks up each request, pulls the deal's scoring and call history, calculates margin, and drafts a reasoned reply; you approve, correct, or overrule it. So the job is two things at once: the reviewer who decides live deals, and the person who builds & improves the AI-based deal desk agent

Your responsibilities

  • Own the day-to-day approval flow for non-standard pricing, discounts, and commercial terms, acting as the fast, consistent escalation point for reps without slowing deals down.

  • Build and evolve pricing governance, including discount rules, approval thresholds, and playbooks, converting recurring exceptions into documented policy.

  • Drive deal health across the funnel: discount discipline, price realization, deal structure, and win rate by segment, diagnosing where deals leak value and fixing it.

  • Translate customer segmentation into differentiated pricing guidance and deal strategies, partnering with Sales to get it applied in real deals, and getting it into the ruleset so it's applied consistently.

  • Coach reps on pricing confidence and value-based selling

  • Partner with Customer Success to adapt the pricing and deal playbook for consistency after the sale.

About you

  • Proven experience in a deal desk, pricing, commercial, revenue operations, or sales-strategy role, ideally in B2B SaaS or fintech. Experience standing up or scaling a deal desk or pricing process from scratch is a plus.

  • Strong analytical toolkit, including SQL and/or advanced spreadsheet modeling.

  • The ability to leverage AI to build a scalable Pricing Deal Desk model, or the appetite to learn it. The direction is a low-touch desk: the agent executes the rules, its output gets better as you correct it, and each additional deal costs less human attention than the last

  • Fluent in English; German or Dutch is a plus.

In addition, here are the skills and attributes we are looking for:

  • Comfortable holding the line with Sales on discount governance while staying a genuine partner to the team.

  • A critical eye for AI output. The agent is sometimes confidently wrong, and catching that before a rep acts on it is part of the job.

  • Brings commercial judgment: understands how reps sell and how price sensitivity shifts across customer segments.

  • Structured and high-ownership, at ease in a fast, low-process, high-change environment.

  • Able to move fluidly between detailed data analysis and higher-level strategic thinking.

About Moss

Moss is the Finance AI platform for Europe's mid-sized businesses, giving companies real-time visibility and full control over their spend. By automating card issuing, invoice management and expenses, Moss simplifies financial workflows and frees finance and accounting teams from manual, administrative work.

Founded in Berlin and used by more than 5,000 businesses including Flink, Schufa, Gusto and Auto1, Moss has raised €200+ million to date and operates in Germany, the Netherlands, the UK and further EU markets. Moss is backed by the most renowned tech investors including Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Global Founders Capital, Cherry Ventures, A-Star and Portage.

We have a team of 300+ people from 50+ nationalities in 5 offices across Europe. Be part of a culture that thrives on impact and speed, where you can take bold moves, learn fast and accomplish more. We’re a place where you can fast track your career - here's what else to expect:

  • Top-of-market compensation package, including equity. 

  • Our vibrant offices are at the heart of our culture, where in-person time fuels collaboration and connection over weekly breakfasts and Friday demos.

  • Additional benefits include: 20 days “work from abroad”, 600EUR/GBP Learning & Development Budget, and other local benefits.

Unless stated otherwise, benefits apply to full-time positions (interns and working students receive a tailored package).

By applying for the above position, you will confirm that you have reviewed and agreed to our Data Privacy Policy.

title: Senior Python Engineer, Platform Libraries (m/f/d)
description:
The role

We’re looking for a Senior Python Engineer, Platform Libraries (m/f/d) to join our team and play a key role in developing software that connects and translates lab equipment hardware interfaces, automates machines, and powers our next-generation automation platform. As a core team member, you will be working on cutting-edge technology, building software that bridges the gap between software and hardware, enabling seamless integration across various vendors.

Connectors are how we do it. Every instrument we bring online gets one, and every connector is built on our shared Python libraries: Bus, our Connector Development Kit, and the stack underneath them.

Our mission is to empower researchers and engineers by bridging the gap between lab equipment and cloud-based automation. Our customers are solving critical challenges like curing diseases, developing sustainable materials, and addressing global food security. We provide them with the tools to connect their devices, automate workflows, and unlock new possibilities in R&D.

Your mandate has two halves. Own the libraries as a product with real users, our own engineers today and external contributors later. And stay close enough to customer connector work that what you build is grounded in problems that actually exist.


Why you'll love this role

Your users are engineers. Your success lets other people ship connectors faster. That's a different craft from shipping features, and it's the one we're hiring for.

Real hardware, real failure modes. Instruments time out, return garbage, and arrive with documentation that's wrong. You'll debug against physical devices in our Munich workshop.


Open source on purpose. Our CDK and our standardization work (SiLA 2) are public. What you build gets used and criticized by people outside the company.


Senior scope, small team. You'll be the person who decides how connector engineering works here. No layer between you and that decision.


Your mission

1. The Builder: own the shared libraries

  • Own Bus, the CDK, and the core stack. Features, tests, CI, releases, and deprecations across the connectors already running in production.

  • Extract abstractions from real work. When the same pattern shows up in the third connector, it becomes a library feature. You're the one who notices, and the one who does it.

  • Make the docs good enough to remove yourself. An outside contributor should be able to build a connector on our libraries without a call.

  • Set the quality standard. You define what "tested" means before a connector reaches a customer, and you make it stick.

2. The Shipper: build connectors on real instruments

  • Ship production connectors end to end. Spec sheet, physical device, protocol, proof of connectivity, tested connector, live customer. Independently.

  • Reverse-engineer what isn't documented. Roughly half the instruments we touch have incomplete or wrong docs. Packet captures, trial and error, vendor calls.

  • Work with the workshop. Our Connector Factory team gets instruments development-ready. You take it from there.

  • Talk to the people who use it. Automation engineers and scientists at biotech and pharma customers. Their constraints shape what the libraries need next.


Your profile

  • Deep Python: 5+ years of writing production Python other people depend on. Async, typing, packaging, testing. You've designed APIs that other engineers built on, not just glue code.

  • You've debugged a real protocol against real hardware: gRPC, serial, TCP, OPC UA, CAN, USB. Which one matters less than having sat with a packet capture and a device that won't respond.

  • You ship without a spec: When the documentation is wrong, you reverse-engineer, instead of filing a vendor ticket and waiting. 

  • You build for other developers: An SDK, a library, an internal platform. Something where your job was making other engineers faster.

  • Located in Munich: The instruments are physically here at WERK1. 


Nice to have

  • SiLA 2, or another device abstraction and interoperability standard

  • Lab automation, scientific instruments, or a life science background

  • Open source maintainership with actual external contributors

  • C, C++, .NET, or Rust, for the vendor DLLs and drivers we end up wrapping

  • Docker, Kubernetes, edge deployment

  • German, for vendor conversations


Probably not a fit if

Better to say this now than in week 6.


  • Your Python is all APIs and databases and you've never debugged a physical device.

  • You'd want two quarters to redesign the library architecture before shipping a connector.

  • You like shipping integrations but have no appetite for going back afterwards to generalise, test, and document.

  • You want the library work without the customer deadlines. Both are in the job.


About UniteLabs

UniteLabs is on the mission to accelerate scientific progress by automating lab processes with scalable infrastructure.

We’re a startup based in Munich, Germany, pioneering an industry-first integration platform for lab automation, bridging hardware and software across vendor barriers to revolutionize life science R&D. By digitalizing life science R&D, we enable researchers in biotech, pharma, chemistry, and food industries to accelerate their work in groundbreaking fields such as disease treatment, sustainable materials, and food security.

Our platform empowers customers to analyze more data, run autonomous experiments, and leverage AI-driven solutions, driving innovation and efficiency. At UniteLabs, we are committed to providing the infrastructure that powers the future of scientific discovery.

As one of the first full-time hires, you'll thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and take on significant responsibilities from day one. We are a tech-driven company that takes pride in our solutions—and we’re looking for individuals who share that passion and want to grow with the company into leadership and expert roles.


Why You’ll Love Working Here

  • Impactful Work: Work on meaningful products in an ambitious, supportive environment as part of a team revolutionizing connectivity in laboratory automation to enable breakthroughs in science and technology.

  • Work with the Best: Join a talented, ambitious team in a dynamic, transparent environment where your ideas help shape the company's future.

  • Collaborative Culture: Team-oriented environment focused on continuous knowledge-sharing and professional growth, with regular team-building activities including offsites and work-cations.

  • Flexible Environment: Backed by an employee-first culture that supports flexible remote work and PTO, with our main office in the vibrant WERK1 Munich hub. Hardware debugging happens there, so being regularly onsite is a must.

  • Attractive Compensation Package: Competitive compensation with growth potential in a VC-backed startup, along with a laptop of choice, annual productivity budget, and a growing list of benefits for sports, mobility, insurance, and more.


Tech stack

A non-exhaustive list of our main technologies and tools used for a given task:

  • Connectors: Python, SiLA 2, gRPC, zeroconf

  • Workflows: Python, Prefect

  • Services: TypeScript, NestJS, Prisma

  • Web: TypeScript, Vue 3, Nuxt 3, TailwindCSS

  • Cloud: Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, AWS, Terraform

  • Databases: PostgreSQL


How to apply

If you’re passionate about automation, have a customer-focused mindset, and are ready to define the future of smart labs, we’d love to hear from you. Share your CV or LinkedIn profile, along with your responses to the three questions in the application form.

Let’s build the future of lab automation together. Apply today!

title: Forward Deployed Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
⭐️ Your Impact:

The European trades are one of the least digitised industries left. Software
penetration sits under 15%, against roughly 70% in the US. The labour
productivity gap runs about 30%. Millions of skilled people spend their evenings
on paperwork instead of the craft they trained for — in the industry that has to
deliver the energy transition.

There is almost no incumbent software to displace. That is unusual, and it won't
last.

smalt replaces the back office entirely rather than selling Meister another tool
to manage. In the last six months that went from a partner app and a dashboard
to around thirty AI agents in production - pricing real jobs, qualifying real
leads, running the operations of businesses whose payroll depends on it working.

These days building thirty agents is easy. Knowing which thirty is what's challenging.

That only comes from being in the Betrieb and talking to the Handwerker.

That's what this role is for.

What you'll do

You'll sit in Handwerksbetrieben - at the Meister's desk, in the van, on site, next to our team -
and watch how the work actually happens. Then you'll come back and build the
thing that fixes it, often multiple times on the same day.

- Spend real time with partners. Not a quarterly customer call. You'll know
  our Meister by name, understand their P&L, and notice the thing they've
  stopped complaining about because they assume it can't be fixed.
- Build across the stack. Python/FastAPI services, Vue interfaces, Flutter
  screens, agent loops, data pipelines - whatever the problem needs.
- Own agents in production. Not demos. Agents that price real jobs, answer
  real customers, and cost real money when they're wrong. Reliability,
  evaluation, structured output, graceful failure.
- Decide what to build. You'll write your own acceptance criteria. Nobody
  here will hand you a spec, and waiting for one is how to fail in this
  role.
- Measure whether it worked. Hours saved per partner, offers that go out
  untouched, leads answered before a competitor picks up. If the number didn't
  move, it didn't work.

What that looks like in practice

In July one of our Meister got an early build of the partner app, ahead of the
general rollout. He tested it between jobs and sent screenshots: from a calendar
appointment he could no longer jump into the project to pull the customer's
phone number. He had a reply in two minutes. Within the hour he'd also asked for
a navigation button - tap the address, go straight to maps.

Neither was news. Both were already being worked on before he hit send.

We aim to be fast, and close enough to the work that we've usually seen the problem before the person living it has to tell us.



✨ What Makes You a Great Fit:

You might be a great fit if you

- Have owned something end to end - architecture through delivery through the
  unglamorous iteration afterwards. We don't count years; we look at what you
  carried.
- Get obsessed with a problem rather than a stack. The tools change every few
  months. The curiosity compounds.
- Would rather ship something that changes a tradesperson's week than win an
  argument about abstractions.
- Actually like talking to customers, and have changed your mind about a feature
  because of something a user said.
- Are comfortable being the least knowledgeable person in a room full of
  electricians, and ask the question anyway.
- Can hold "ship it today" and "this needs to survive two years" in your head at
  the same time, and know which one applies.

Our stack, so you know what you're walking into:

- Backend: Python, FastAPI, async SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL (with pgvector), Celery, Redis
- Frontend: Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite, PrimeVue
- Mobile: Flutter
- AI: Anthropic, Open source and Google models, vector search over partner and catalog data
- Infra: Google Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Sentry

We care that you're strong somewhere and unafraid everywhere else. If you've
never written Vue but you've shipped production systems and you learn fast, that
is fine - several of us hadn't either.

What we do look for:

- Production experience with LLM-powered features, and the scars that come with it: evaluation, structured output parsing, context management, error recovery
- A track record of shipping things people actually used
- High agency. You'll get context and constraints, not instructions.
- Raw intelligence paired with a humble mindset

German is helpful and you'll pick some up either way - our partners speak it all day. It isn't a requirement but definitely a nice to have. The the team works in English.


☀️ Why You'll Love Working With Us:

- Top-of-market compensation and a meaningful VSOP package
- Direct access to real users and short feedback loops
- Real ownership, and direct proximity to the founders - and to General
  Catalyst, noa, Owl Ventures and Heartfelt
- A team of five engineers who have shipped more in six months than most teams
  do in two years, and who set the pace themselves

title: UVC Partners: Data & AI - Master Thesis / Internship (f/m/x)
description:
About us

UVC Partners is one of Europe’s leading early-stage venture capital firms. With our fourth fund generation of €250 million, we invest in disruptive B2B startups at the seed and Series A stage across Europe. Our focus areas include enterprise software, mobility, and industrial technologies.
Headquartered in Munich and closely integrated with UnternehmerTUM, Europe’s largest entrepreneurship center, we are proud partners to some of Europe’s most ambitious founders – including Flixbus, Isar Aerospace, finn.auto, Proxima Fusion, and Aleph Alpha.

At UVC Partners, we’re driven by a deep passion for entrepreneurship and its power to positively shape society. Environmental and social responsibility are core to our DNA. We hold ourselves to the highest standards in everything we do. As a firm, we continuously reinvent ourselves to stay ahead and best serve our portfolio and investors. We believe in ownership over hierarchy and foster a culture built on collaboration, curiosity, and personal engagement. And while we’re serious about our mission, we also genuinely enjoy working together and building lasting relationships along the way.


Your mission

You will join a specialized team working at the intersection of applied research and venture capital, side by side with investors, AI researchers, and engineers building the backbone of our investment intelligence. This is a hands-on role with real stakes. You will be treated as a full member of the team, expected to take a research question from literature to a working prototype and to present your results to the people who make the investment decisions.


Your profile

  • You are enrolled in a Master’s program in Computer Science, Data Science, Data Engineering, Information Systems, or a similar program at a top university.
  • You bring depth, or the ambition to build it, in at least one relevant toolkit, whether that is graph ML and graph databases (e.g. PyTorch Geometric), LLM tooling, tool use and evaluation, or probabilistic modeling (e.g. PyMC, NumPyro).
  • You write clean, modular Python and have firm machine learning and statistics fundamentals.
  • You are fluent with AI-assisted coding tools and you have judgment about them. You know what they do well, where they quietly fail, and you review everything they produce. You do not ship AI slop.
  • You work independently. You have run a project where you set the direction yourself, and you can point to it.
  • You are fluent in English, including technical language. It is what you will work, write, and present in. German is helpful but not required.

How we work
We are an AI-powered development team. Everyone here codes with AI assistance, and we treat that as a craft. You need to know which parts of a problem to hand over, where these tools fail quietly, and how to review output you did not write.
Agency matters a lot in our team. You get mentorship, context, and access to everyone. You do not get someone assigning you tasks every morning. Take a rough problem statement, come back with an approach, show drafts while they can still change, and flag what is not working. What you bring should outweigh what it costs us to support you.

Potential Research Directions
These are directions we could explore, with scope defined together at the start based on your background and where the work leads.
1. With Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) we would work on a graph-structured database, where people and companies are nodes and the relationships between them are part of the data, and ask what that structure can tell us that a table cannot.
2. With Program-aided Language Models (PAL) we would have the model write a small program for every number it pulls from decks and financial statements, so figures are accurately computed, because that is what makes it safe to point a language model at financial data.
3. And with Bayesian Updating we would keep our recorded understanding of a company moving as new evidence arrives, since the investment process is iterative and a view written down two years ago should not still be the view today. Your thesis could focus on one of these, though as a full-time member of the team you will work across several.

Academic Supervision: The Lead of the Data & AI Team is a PhD candidate at TUM's School of Computation, Information and Technology (CIT) and can supervise CIT masters students directly, so there is no separate supervisor search. However, you are free to choose your own supervisor and candidates from other universities bring their own.


What we offer

  • Network: A desk at the Munich Urban Colab, our main office, with the option of a second one in Garching, plus access to the UnternehmerTUM ecosystem of startups, experts, and investors.
  • Team & Culture: Monthly team lunches, our regular Stammtisch, free sports classes, Makerspace access for your personal projects, and regular team events.
  • Compensation: An attractive salary for the full six months of your master thesis or internship.
  • Ownership: Research that is yours end to end and feeds real fund decisions.
  • Equipment: A MacBook or a Windows laptop, whichever you work best on.
  • AI Tooling: Full access to the AI development stack we use daily, and a team that will teach you to use it properly.
  • Real Data: Proprietary venture data that researchers rarely get access to, with the pipelines to use it productively.

Interested?
Please send a one-page CV, a current transcript, and a link to your GitHub or portfolio. Tell us which of these directions interests you most and why. We look forward to hearing from you!
